title: Forensics: analysis with Autopsy, winhex and memory dumps

videos.script: Lesson 16 made an image of the file server's disk and put it away. This lesson opens a copy of it. {{open}} A disk has layers: names, the records behind the names, and the bytes. Deleting a file removes the name. The rest stays. {{layers}} You will find a file somebody deleted, bring it back whole, and prove it with a hash. {{recover}} You will read the raw bytes, the way a hex editor shows them, and build a timeline from the file system's own clocks. And then memory, which holds what a disk never sees. {{memory}} Every finding is something you can show somebody else, and they can check it from the same image.
